--- title: bc.cplx format: html: css: /man.css --- ## Broadcasted Complex Numeric Operations {.unnumbered} ### Description The bc.cplx() method performs broadcasted complex numeric operations on pairs of arrays.

### Usage 
bc.cplx(x, y, op, ...)

## S4 method for signature 'ANY'
bc.cplx(x, y, op)
### Arguments
x, y conformable vectors/arrays of type complex.
Numeric and logical arrays will be coerced to type complex.
op a single string, giving the operator.
Supported arithmetic operators: +, -, *, /.
Supported relational operators: ==, !=.
... further arguments passed to or from methods.

### Details For the * and / operators, bc.cplx() uses more strict NA checks than base 'R':
If for an iteration, re(x), im(x), re(y), and/or im(y) contains NA, than the result for that iteration is necessarily NA_complex_. ### Value For arithmetic operators:
A complex array as a result of the broadcasted arithmetic operation.

For relational operators:
A logical array as a result of the broadcasted relational comparison.

### See Also [broadcast_operators](aaa01_broadcast_operators.qmd)
### Examples ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library("broadcast") x.dim <- c(4:2) x.len <- prod(x.dim) gen <- function() sample(c(rnorm(20), NA, NaN, Inf, -Inf)) x <- array(gen() + gen() * -1i, x.dim) y <- array(gen() + gen() * -1i, c(4,1,1)) bc.cplx(x, y, "==") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE NA NA #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE NA FALSE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE FALSE NA #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE NA #> [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE bc.cplx(x, y, "!=") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE NA NA #> [2,] TRUE
